sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a Boca Raton property?
sections.html:
The quickest path is typically a cash buyer who accepts the property as-is, since a listing adds showings, appraisals and buyer financing. Boca Raton homes range from older single-family streets to condominiums, so the right path depends on the property type and what the building association requires.

  • Cash buyer: few contingencies, with a closing day you set together.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, plus repair requests and lender deadlines.
  • Owner sale: you manage the contract and the closing agent.

sections.h2: What kind of housing market is Boca Raton?
sections.html:
Only one other city in Palm Beach County is larger than Boca Raton, and the city's comprehensive plan traces a path from coastal resort town, incorporated in 1925, to high-tech center. The plan states that over 75 percent of the housing stock was built after 1970.

The same plan, adopted in July 2020 and amended in January 2025, charts median single-family prices rising from $268,000 in 2000 to $502,272 in 2019 and says fewer median income earners can afford preferred housing. It counted 91,797 permanent residents in 2017 and projects 101,652 full-time and seasonal residents by 2040. The plan counts both year-round and seasonal residents in that projection, so ask your agent or buyer how timing fits the local season.

sections.h2: What city rules affect a Boca Raton house sale?
sections.html:
Boca Raton enforces housing standards through code enforcement, and its plan commits to systematic housing inspections focused on areas with older structures. Historic homes fall under the city's Historic Preservation Ordinance, so any rehab or demolition plan for an older house should start with the city.

  • The Community Appearance Board enforces upkeep standards, mainly for commercial and industrial property.
  • Mobile homes are permitted in all single-family zoning districts, per the plan.
  • The city runs periodic bulk trash pickups, which helps when you clear out a house before listing.
  • New projects of ten or more units may need to provide 10 percent workforce housing or pay in lieu, if the city adopts the rule.

The plan also says the city assists owners of historically significant housing in applying for state and federal assistance programs, and it sets a workforce housing target range of 80 percent up to 140 percent of area median income for the West Palm Beach-Boca Raton-Boynton Beach area. The Boca Raton Housing Authority supports residents earning below the median.

For open permits, ask the city's Planning, Zoning and Building staff. The county property appraiser says the city or county permitting agency, not the appraiser, owns permit and situs address records.

sections.h2: How does the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser value a Boca Raton home?
sections.html:
The appraiser sets three numbers for each parcel: just value, which is market value; assessed value, which is just value less caps such as Save Our Homes; and taxable value, which is assessed value less exemptions. The tax collector uses taxable value to bill you.

Values are fixed each January 1, and the appraiser says it inspects every property at least every five years through site visits or aerial photos. The appraiser's site offers a property tax calculator on each parcel page where a buyer enters a purchase price and whether they will homestead, so buyers can estimate their own bill before making an offer.

sections.h2: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell in Boca Raton?
sections.html:
The exemption belongs to you, so it travels to your next home while the buyer must file their own. If you sell during the year, it may stay on the property until the next January 1, but the appraiser notes that it is then not the new owner's exemption.

Portability lets you carry Save Our Homes savings to a new Florida homestead, and the county page says you have a three tax year window to port after losing a homestead. State guidance says to file the portability form with the homestead application by March 1, and the new homestead must be set up within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned. Rental limits matter if the house sits empty or is rented before the sale: the county says renting on January 1 loses the exemption, and renting more than six months counts as abandonment.

Changing the name on the deed can also remove a homestead, which is why transfers to an heir should be reviewed first.

sections.h2: What do condominium and commercial owners in Boca Raton need to check?
sections.html:
Condo sellers should ask the association about assessments before listing. The appraiser says that if Florida's SB-4-D building safety law affects the market for condominiums, it will value those properties accordingly and review assessment fee effects case by case.

Boca Raton, along with Boynton Beach and West Palm Beach, charges a Fire Rescue Assessment on commercial property based on use and square footage, which the appraiser says can exceed $10,000 for some properties. Landlords and small commercial owners should get that figure from the county before agreeing to any price.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with transferring a Boca Raton deed?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration on a deed in Palm Beach County, and all parties to the deed are liable to the state. The city's housing plan also notes support for a documentary surtax program under the Sadowski Act, which funds affordable housing, so ask the clerk what applies to your deed.

Statute adds page-based recording charges at the clerk, and the deed needs two subscribing witnesses. If you dispute an assessment, you can ask the appraiser for an informal review at 561.355.3230 or petition the Value Adjustment Board run by the county clerk.

sections.h2: What if my Boca Raton house is damaged or behind on payments?
sections.html:
Storm damage affects a tax bill the year after it happens, because values follow the condition on January 1. A home that is uninhabitable for more than 30 days may qualify for a partial refund, and a rebuilt home that stays within 110 percent of the original square footage can keep its homestead after a calamity.

If a mortgage is behind, the Florida foreclosure statute lets the court order a public sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, with a 5 percent bidder deposit, and any surplus is handled through the clerk. Talk to a Florida attorney or housing counselor early so you know your choices before a sale date is set.

faqs.q: Is Boca Raton in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Yes. Boca Raton is in Palm Beach County and its property records are kept by the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, with billing handled by the county's tax collector.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The county says exemptions move with the owner, so the buyer files their own, and the sale resets assessed value to market on the next January 1.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate on a Boca Raton deed?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Miami-Dade is the only county with a different rate, and every party to the deed is liable to the state.

faqs.q: Can I rent out my Boca Raton house and keep homestead?
faqs.a: Only within limits. Renting 30 days or less in a year is allowed, longer rentals risk the exemption, renting on January 1 loses it, and more than six months is abandonment.

faqs.q: How do I dispute a Boca Raton assessment?
faqs.a: Start with an informal review by calling the appraiser at 561.355.3230. If the issue remains, petition the Value Adjustment Board through the county clerk.
